0. FOREWORD
adopted by the Indian Standards Institution the draft finalized by the Oils and Oilseeds approved by the Chemical Division Council Products Division Council.

0.1 This Indian Standard was on 16 November 1981, after Sectional Committee had been and the Agricultural and Food

0.2 NAHOR kernels are obtained from seeds of NAHOH ( Mesua jkren Linn. ) tree. NAHOR trees grow in large number in the evergreen forests of Assam, West Bengal, Western Ghats, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala In the cultivated condition, it is found chiefly as an and Andamans. ornamental tree under various local names. The flowering season of the tree is February to March which extends up to April and May in some places, The fruits are borne two months later. The fruit is 2.5 to 30 mm long, void or hemispherical, reddish in colour and it contains 1 to 4 seeds. 0.3 NAHOR seed kernels ore rich in oil having 55 to 77 percent oil of yellow to brown colour with an unpleasant pungent odour. The oil is used, The oil is suitable for soap at present, mostly for lighting purposes. making but the odour and colour of the oil are imparted to the soap. It may, however, be properly utilized for soap making after processing. The oil is said to have some medicinal properties also. 0.4 The requirements `IS: 8896-1978'. for oil obtained from NAHOR kernels is covered in
